prompt: Which statement correctly defines precision according to the Cambridge 9702 syllabus?
options: The closeness of a measured value to the true value of the quantity.
The degree of agreement among repeated measurements, indicated by their spread or range.
The smallest change in a quantity that a measuring instrument can distinguish.
The difference between an experimental mean and a trusted reference standard.

answer.explanation: Precision is defined as the degree of agreement among repeated measurements, indicated by their spread or range.

distractor_explanations: This is the definition of accuracy, not precision.
Correct. Precision is indicated by the spread or range of repeated readings under the same conditions.
This describes measurement error or systematic offset.
hints: Precision is about how close repeated measurements are to each other.
Recall the controlled syllabus wording: spread or range.
solution: Precision is the degree of agreement among repeated measurements, indicated by their spread or range.
teacher_walkthrough: Recall the controlled definition: the degree of agreement among repeated measurements, indicated by their spread or range.

provenance.independence_statement: Authored to test verbatim recall of the Cambridge definition of precision.
